My Day in the Hospital.q: How long is Nurse Sarah's shift in the article?
My Day in the Hospital.e: The article says she has coffee before her 12-hour shift begins.

My Day in the Hospital.q: What does Sarah do as soon as she arrives at the hospital?
o: She administers medication to all patients
She checks patients' charts and reviews updates
My Day in the Hospital.e: The text says she checks patients' charts and reviews updates from the night shift on arrival.

My Day in the Hospital.q: Why does Mr. Ramy need extra attention?
o: He has been recovering from surgery.
He was a car accident victim.
My Day in the Hospital.e: The text says the elderly Mr. Ramy has been recovering from surgery and needs extra attention.

My Day in the Hospital.q: The nurse has to ______ the medicine to the patient every six hours.
My Day in the Hospital.e: To administer means to give medicine or treatment to someone.

My Day in the Hospital.q: Helping sick children is a ______ job; it gives you a feeling of satisfaction.
My Day in the Hospital.e: Rewarding means giving a feeling of satisfaction because you helped someone.

My Day in the Hospital.q: Sarah calls nursing a "never-ending rollercoaster" because it ______ .
o: has many emotional ups and downs
My Day in the Hospital.e: A rollercoaster is a situation or experience with many ups and downs, often emotional.

My Day in the Hospital.q: When the accident victim arrived, the team "sprang into action". This means they ______ .
My Day in the Hospital.e: The idiom 'spring into action' means to suddenly begin working or responding quickly.

My Day in the Hospital.q: After the fire alarm, there was complete ______ in the building; nobody knew where to go.
My Day in the Hospital.e: Chaos is a state of complete confusion and disorder.

Emergency Call.q: The nurse put two fingers on the man's wrist to check his ______ .
Emergency Call.e: The pulse is the regular beating of the heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck.

Emergency Call.q: The old man felt very weak and suddenly ______ on the floor.
Emergency Call.e: To collapse means to fall down suddenly, usually because of illness or weakness.

o: medical professionals who give emergency care and take people to hospital
doctors who work only in clinics
Emergency Call.e: Paramedics give emergency care and take people to hospital by ambulance.

Emergency Call.q: CPR is an emergency procedure that ______ .
o: uses chest compressions when the heart has stopped
takes an X-ray of the chest
Emergency Call.e: CPR uses chest compressions to help someone whose heart has stopped.

Emergency Call.q: The patient lost ______ and did not answer when the doctor called his name.
Emergency Call.e: Consciousness is the state of being awake and aware of what is happening around you.

Emergency Call.q: She ______ her bag quickly and ran to catch the bus.
Emergency Call.e: To grab means to take or hold something quickly and strongly.

Emergency Call.q: The "chest" is the part of the body ______ .
o: between the neck and the stomach
at the back of the head
between the hand and the elbow
Emergency Call.e: The chest is the front part of the body between the neck and the stomach.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: Doctors ______ more than fifty patients so far today.
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: Present perfect simple (have/has + p.p.) is used for completed actions with a present result, often with 'today/so far'.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: I'm exhausted because I ______ in the emergency room since 6 a.m.
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: Present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) stresses the duration of an action continuing until now.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: Choose the passive: "They have opened a new clinic in our village."
o: A new clinic has opened in our village.
A new clinic has been opened in our village.
A new clinic have been opened in our village.
A new clinic was been opened in our village.
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: The present perfect passive is object + have/has + been + past participle.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: She ______ the head nurse for ten years, so they are close friends.
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: 'Know' is a state verb, so we use present perfect simple, not the continuous form.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: How many times ______ that hospital this year?
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: Present perfect simple is used for 'how many times/how much'.
Plural subject + haven't + been + past participle is the negative present perfect passive.

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: Which form is correct for the Present Perfect Continuous?
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: The book gives the form have/has + been + present participle (-ing).

Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.q: His clothes are wet because he ______ the car.
Tired Hands, Caring Hearts.e: Present perfect continuous is used for a recently finished action with a visible result now.

Beyond the White Coat.q: Why was Dr. Basem "soaked to the skin" when he arrived?
o: He fell into a swimming pool.
A patient threw water at him.
Beyond the White Coat.e: It was raining cats and dogs, so he was completely wet from head to toe.
The text says the child had swallowed a coin.

Beyond the White Coat.q: How did the team help the toddler?
o: They gave him CPR for an hour.
They removed the coin using a flexible scope.
They sent him to another hospital.
Beyond the White Coat.e: Using a flexible scope, the team carefully removed the coin.

Beyond the White Coat.q: Which word best describes Nurse Noura during the emergencies?
Beyond the White Coat.e: The text describes Nurse Noura as calm under pressure, giving clear and confident instructions.

Beyond the White Coat.q: The worker was "pale as a ghost". This means he was ______ .
o: extremely pale from fear, shock or illness
Beyond the White Coat.e: 'Pale as a ghost' means extremely pale, usually because of fear, shock, or illness.

Beyond the White Coat.q: The worker ______ his bleeding hand, trying not to cry out.
Beyond the White Coat.e: In the text the construction worker clutched (held tightly) his bleeding hand.

Beyond the White Coat.q: Dr. Maha prepared to stitch a deep cut on the man's ______ .
Beyond the White Coat.e: The text says Dr. Maha prepared to stitch a deep cut on his forehead.

Beyond the White Coat.q: According to the Comprehension Tip, the main idea is often found in ______ .
Beyond the White Coat.e: The tip says the central theme is often found in the introduction or conclusion.

My Blog Post.q: What is the purpose of a catchy title in a blog post?
o: to make people want to click and read
My Blog Post.e: The book says the catchy title's purpose is to make people want to click and read.

My Blog Post.q: How many paragraphs should the main body of a blog post usually have?
My Blog Post.e: The book says the main body is usually 2-4 paragraphs.

My Blog Post.q: The conclusion of a blog post should ______ .
o: summarize the main points and give a final thought
introduce the topic for the first time
My Blog Post.e: The conclusion's purpose is to summarize your main points and give a final thought.

My Blog Post.q: The style of a blog post is usually ______ .
My Blog Post.e: Blog posts are usually informal or semi-formal, like talking to a friend.

My Blog Post.q: In the draft "My Unwelcome Visitor", who or what is the unwelcome visitor?
My Blog Post.e: The blog post is about 'A Recent Cold Experience'; the writer had a severe viral cold.

My Blog Post.q: "Have you ever had a very bad cold? Let me know in the comments!" This part of the blog post is the ______ .
My Blog Post.e: It ends the post with a final thought and a question to readers, as conclusions do.

o: a piece of writing published on an online journal or website
a formal letter to a company
My Blog Post.e: The book defines a blog post as writing published on a blog, an online journal or website.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: Which simple machines did ancient Egyptians rely on to build pyramids and temples?
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: The text says ancient Egyptians relied heavily on simple machines like levers and ramps.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: During the Industrial Revolution, Egypt imported advanced machinery from ______ .
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: The text says Egypt began importing advanced machinery from Europe.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: What was one negative result of the new machines during the Industrial Revolution?
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: The text says not all changes were smooth; some traditional crafts disappeared as machines took over.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: How do museums in Egypt blend old and new today?
o: They replace old statues with robots.
They use steam engines to move artifacts.
They use 3D scanning to preserve ancient artifacts.
They sell artifacts to private companies.
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: Museums now use 3D scanning to preserve ancient artifacts, blending old and new.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: Our school has a ______ computer lab with the latest advanced technology.
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: Sophisticated means complex or advanced in design or technology.

o: a ruling family that holds power for several generations
a machine that separates cotton from seeds
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: The book defines dynasty as a ruling family holding power for several generations.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: Early scientists "laid the groundwork" for modern medicine. This means they ______ .
o: built the ground floor of hospitals
made the preparations needed for later success
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: 'Lay the groundwork' means to make the preparations necessary for something to succeed later.

Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.q: The engineer said, "Machines are tools, not replacements for human skills." He means that machines ______ .
o: should help people, not take their place
Machines in Egypt: Past and Present.e: The engineer argued machines enhance productivity and are tools, not replacements for human skills.

Technical Support Call.q: Your printer won't work if the correct ______ are not installed on the computer.
Technical Support Call.e: Drivers are software that helps devices work.
Offline means not connected to the network.

Technical Support Call.q: The technician tried to ______ the problem step by step.
Technical Support Call.e: To troubleshoot means to fix problems step by step.

Technical Support Call.q: The patient was taken to hospital with great ______ because his condition was serious.
Technical Support Call.e: Urgency means importance requiring rapid action.

Technical Support Call.q: Please download the latest ______ of the app; the old one has problems.
Technical Support Call.e: A version is one form of something slightly different from other forms of the same thing.

Technical Support Call.q: Wires used to connect devices are called ______ .
Technical Support Call.e: The book defines cables as wires used to connect devices.
Right-click means press the right mouse button.

The Role of Machines.q: Dr. Ali said, "Machines help people work faster." In reported speech: Dr. Ali said that machines ______ people work faster.
The Role of Machines.e: In reported statements the present usually changes to the past.

The Role of Machines.q: The manager said, "We use robots in our factory." Reported: The manager said that ______ robots in their factory.
The Role of Machines.e: We change pronouns (we -> they) and the present tense to the past.

The Role of Machines.q: She said, "They have built a new machine." Reported: She said that they ______ a new machine.
The Role of Machines.e: When reporting, the present perfect moves back to the past perfect.

The Role of Machines.q: The guard said, "Don't take photos inside the museum." Reported: The guard told us ______ photos inside the museum.
The Role of Machines.e: Negative commands are reported with object + not to + infinitive.

The Role of Machines.q: "Could you check the system?" he said to me. Reported: He asked me ______ the system.
The Role of Machines.e: Requests are reported with asked + object + to + infinitive.

The Role of Machines.q: The supervisor said, "Turn off the machine!" Reported: The supervisor ______ me to turn off the machine.
The Role of Machines.e: Commands are reported with told/ordered/asked + object + to + infinitive.

The Role of Machines.q: In reported statements, the word "that" after said/told/explained is ______ .
The Role of Machines.e: The Language Tip says we often use 'that' after reporting verbs, but it is optional.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: Which of these is mentioned as a household appliance in the text?
Our Machine-Driven World.e: The text lists washing machines, microwaves and vacuum cleaners as household appliances.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: According to a recent study in the text, most people use ______ every day.
Our Machine-Driven World.e: The text says most people use over five machines every single day.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: What happened in the factory after using automated systems?
Our Machine-Driven World.e: A factory manager said production has doubled since they started using automated systems.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: Smartwatches in the text track our ______ .
o: heart rate, steps and sleep quality
Our Machine-Driven World.e: The text says smartwatches track our heart rate, steps, and sleep quality.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: Why are some people worried, according to the text?
o: We may rely too much on machines.
Our Machine-Driven World.e: Some people worry that we rely too much on machines and life could stop if technology fails.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: After the power cut, all the trains came to a complete ______ .
Our Machine-Driven World.e: To 'come to a standstill' means to stop completely.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: What is the writer's final message about machines?
o: Technology should serve us, not rule us.
Our Machine-Driven World.e: The text ends: technology should serve us, not rule us.

Our Machine-Driven World.q: When you meet an unfamiliar word, the Context Clues tip advises you to ______ .
o: look at the surrounding words and sentences
Our Machine-Driven World.e: The tip says the surrounding words and sentences often give clues to the word's meaning.

For or Against?.q: In an argumentative essay, the writer ______ .
o: gives a claim, supports it, and answers the opposite view
For or Against?.e: You give your claim with reasons and evidence, mention the opposite claim and say why yours is stronger.

For or Against?.q: Where should you state your claim (thesis)?
For or Against?.e: The introduction introduces the topic, gives background and states your claim.

For or Against?.q: "On the other hand, some people think phones are useful for learning." The function of this sentence is ______ .
For or Against?.e: 'On the other hand' is listed as a phrase for introducing the other side.

For or Against?.q: Which phrase is used to refute the other side?
For or Against?.e: 'However, I disagree because...' is a phrase for refuting the other side.

For or Against?.q: The conclusion of an argumentative essay should ______ .
o: mention the opposite side for the first time
restate your claim and summarize your main points
For or Against?.e: The conclusion restates your claim and summarizes your main points.

For or Against?.q: Which phrase is used for supporting your claim?
For or Against?.e: 'Another reason is...' is in the list of phrases for supporting your claim.

For or Against?.q: In the uniforms essay, "Some people say uniforms limit personal expression. However, ..." is the ______ paragraph.
For or Against?.e: It mentions the opposite side and says why the writer disagrees.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: According to the text, who is largely responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions?
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: The text says industrialized nations are largely responsible for the majority of emissions.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: Who bears the brunt of climate change, according to the text?
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: Low-income and marginalized communities, particularly in the Global South, bear the brunt of its consequences.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: Poor families often "bear the brunt" of rising prices. This means they ______ .
o: suffer the worst part of it
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: 'Bear the brunt' means to suffer the worst part of something bad.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: What does the "Youth Climate Lab" do?
o: It builds factories in the Global South.
It collects taxes from poor nations.
It empowers young innovators to develop climate solutions.
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: The text says it empowers young innovators to develop solutions for climate challenges.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: Which tangible change resulted from young people's efforts?
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: Their efforts resulted in community solar projects and successful recycling campaigns.
The book matches equity with fairness or equal treatment.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: He broke the window, so now he has to "face the music". This means he must ______ .
o: accept the unpleasant results of his actions
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: 'Face the music' means to accept the unpleasant results of your actions.

Climate Justice and Global Activism.q: Which of these is a compound noun?
Climate Justice and Global Activism.e: A compound noun is two nouns used together; carbon footprint is a book example.

An Interview with a Meteorologist.e: The book defines a meteorologist as someone who studies or predicts the weather.

An Interview with a Meteorologist.q: A very long period of dangerously hot weather is called a ______ .
An Interview with a Meteorologist.e: The book defines heat wave as a very long period of dangerously hot weather.

An Interview with a Meteorologist.q: According to the weather ______ , it will rain tomorrow.
An Interview with a Meteorologist.e: A forecast is the prediction of future weather conditions.

An Interview with a Meteorologist.q: The sky was ______ all day: cloudy and grey.
Take a light jacket; it's a bit ______ this evening.
The weather in Alexandria in summer is often ______ : hot and wet.
Someone who is "pessimistic" about the future is ______ .
o: expecting a bad or negative outcome
sure that all will be fine
An Interview with a Meteorologist.e: Pessimistic means expecting a bad or negative outcome.

An Interview with a Meteorologist.q: "It's pouring with rain" means it is ______ .
An Interview with a Meteorologist.e: The weather expression 'pouring with rain' means raining heavily.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: We use "must + base verb" when we are ______ .
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: The Language Tip says must + base verb means 95-100% sure it's true.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: He ______ be at school now; I've just seen him at the club.
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Can't + base verb means we are 95-100% sure it's not true.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: The streets are all wet. It ______ rained last night.
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Must have + past participle means we are nearly certain it happened.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: She ______ the message; she replied to it an hour ago.
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Can't have + past participle means we are certain it did not happen.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: "The state should have invested in sea walls many years ago." This sentence expresses ______ .
o: blame or regret about the past
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Should have + past participle expresses blame or regret in the past.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: It was raining and you got wet. You ______ an umbrella.
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Should have + p.p. is used for blame or regret about something not done in the past.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: Which modal shows only about a 30% possibility in the present?
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: According to the table, might + base verb shows a 30% possibility.

Climate Change and Coastal Cities.q: Fishermen ______ need to change their work methods; we are not sure yet.
Climate Change and Coastal Cities.e: Might + base verb expresses a weak possibility in the present.

Global Climate.q: By how much was global sea level in 2016 higher than the 1983 average?
Global Climate.e: The text says sea level in 2016 was approximately 82 mm higher than the 1983 average.

Global Climate.q: What potential sea level rise is projected by 2100?
Global Climate.e: Projections suggest a potential rise of 0.2 to 2 meters by 2100.

Global Climate.q: What has been the dominant contributor to sea level rise over the past decade?
o: melting of glaciers and ice sheets
Global Climate.e: The text says melting glaciers and ice sheets became the dominant contributor over the past decade.

o: cities are built near the sea
Global Climate.e: The text names thermal expansion of seawater as ocean temperatures increase.

Global Climate.q: About how many people live in low-lying coastal zones exposed to floods?
Global Climate.e: The text estimates 275 million people currently residing in low-lying coastal zones.

Global Climate.q: Which is an example of an adaptation strategy in the text?
Global Climate.e: Amphibious architecture and coastal defense systems are innovative engineering solutions being implemented.

Global Climate.q: Where are most of the world's megacities situated, according to the text?
Global Climate.e: The text says the majority of the world's megacities are situated in coastal areas.

Global Climate.q: The rainbow is a beautiful natural ______ that happens after rain.
Global Climate.e: A phenomenon is a fact or event in nature, as the text uses it for sea level rise.

How to Help Our Environment.q: We use persuasive writing when we want to ______ .
o: convince the reader to take action
How to Help Our Environment.e: The Writing Tip says use persuasive writing to convince the reader to take action.

How to Help Our Environment.q: Which is NOT one of the key characteristics of persuasive writing?
How to Help Our Environment.e: The key characteristics are clear opinion, reasons and evidence, emotional appeal, persuasive language and call to action.

o: tells the reader what to do after reading
How to Help Our Environment.e: The book says a call to action tells the reader what they should do after reading.

How to Help Our Environment.q: "What will happen if we do nothing?" is an example of ______ .
How to Help Our Environment.e: The book gives this as an example of a rhetorical question used in persuasive language.

How to Help Our Environment.q: Emotional appeal uses words that make the reader feel ______ .
How to Help Our Environment.e: Emotional appeal uses words that make the reader feel fear, hope, guilt, or pride.

How to Help Our Environment.q: Which group of words is typical of persuasive language?
How to Help Our Environment.e: The book lists words like must, should, need to, urgent, clearly, obviously.

How to Help Our Environment.q: What is the main message of the article?
o: One person can never make a difference.
Small individual actions together can make a big change.
Climate problems can be solved overnight.
Only governments can help the environment.
How to Help Our Environment.e: The article says if everyone takes small meaningful steps, the combined impact could be huge.

Review 1.q: Nurses at this hospital work an 8-hour ______ .
Review 1.e: A shift is a set period of time that a person works, especially in hospitals.

Review 1.q: Planting trees can help ______ the effects of air pollution.
Review 1.e: To mitigate or reduce means to lessen the bad effects.

Review 1.q: Roads, bridges and power lines are part of a country's ______ .
Review 1.e: Infrastructure is the basic systems and structures a country needs to operate.

Review 1.q: The doctor ______ the patient for two hours, but he still feels pain.
Review 1.e: Present perfect continuous stresses an action continuing over a period up to now.

Review 1.q: He said, "I will call you tomorrow." Reported: He said that he ______ call me the next day.
Review 1.e: In reported speech 'will' changes to 'would' and 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'.

Review 1.q: My mother said, "Don't be late." Reported: My mother told me ______ late.
Review 1.e: Negative commands are reported with told + object + not to + infinitive.

Review 1.q: That ______ be his bag; it's too small for his laptop.
Review 1.e: Can't + base verb shows we are sure something is not true.

Review 1.q: A ______ essay mainly aims to convince the reader and uses emotional appeal.
Review 1.e: Persuasive writing aims to convince and uses emotional appeal and a call to action.

Coral Reefs.q: Why is the coral reef often called a "colorful underwater city"?
o: It has tall buildings under the sea.
It is near big coastal cities.
It is home to thousands of marine species.
Coral Reefs.e: The text says the reef is home to thousands of marine species, from sea turtles to tiny fish.

Coral Reefs.q: Which of these is a threat to coral reefs mentioned in the text?
Coral Reefs.e: Pollution, climate change, and destructive fishing practices pose serious threats to coral reefs.

Coral Reefs.q: What happens to corals when they bleach?
o: They lose their vivid colors and become lifeless.
Coral Reefs.e: When conditions are poor, corals bleach, losing their vivid colors and becoming lifeless.

Coral Reefs.q: "A stitch in time saves nine" means ______ .
o: fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one later
sewing clothes takes a long time
it is too late to act
nine people can solve any problem
Coral Reefs.e: The idiom means fixing a small problem early prevents it from becoming a much bigger problem later.

Coral Reefs.q: Besides supporting marine life, coral reefs also ______ .
o: protect coastal areas from storms and erosion
Coral Reefs.e: The text says reefs protect coastal areas from storms and erosion.

Coral Reefs.q: Be careful with this glass vase; it is very ______ .
Coral Reefs.e: Fragile means easily damaged or broken, as the text says coral reefs are surprisingly fragile.

Coral Reefs.q: Plants ______ in good soil with plenty of water and sunlight.
Coral Reefs.e: To thrive means to grow and do well, as the text hopes reefs will recover and thrive.

Coral Reefs.q: If we don't act now, coral reefs may become "a thing of the past". This means they may ______ .
Coral Reefs.e: 'A thing of the past' means something that no longer exists or is no longer used.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: The book defines hazardous as dangerous or risky.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.q: The fish got ______ in the old fishing net and could not escape.
The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: Entangled means twisted or scrambled together in a complicated way.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.q: Noisy ships can ______ the whales' communication.
The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: To disrupt means to interrupt or break up something, causing disorder.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.q: Scientists use "non-invasive" drones to study whales. "Non-invasive" means ______ .
o: not entering the body or disturbing it
The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: Non-invasive means not entering the body, without instruments going inside.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.q: She is a ______ teacher who gives a lot of time and effort to her students.
The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: Dedicated means giving a lot of time and effort to something because you care about it.

The Ocean's Gentle Giants.q: The whale's ______ song stayed in my mind for days.
The Ocean's Gentle Giants.e: Haunting describes something that stays in your mind, often in a sad or memorable way.
The book defines magnificent as very impressive, beautiful, or splendid.

The Underwater World.e: Number + noun compound adjectives use the singular noun: a three-hour meeting.
Compound adjectives before a noun take a hyphen: a well-known footballer.

The Underwater World.q: As a footballer, Mohamed Salah is ______ .
The Underwater World.e: After a linking verb, hyphens are usually not used.

The Underwater World.q: A device that saves time is a ______ device.
The Underwater World.e: Noun + present participle: a time-saving device.
The Language Tip gives world-famous as noun + adjective.

The Underwater World.q: The man has full confidence in himself. He is a ______ man.
The Underwater World.e: The book's example rewrites this as 'He is a self-confident man.'

The Underwater World.q: We bought a ______ car; nobody had used it before.
The Underwater World.e: Brand-new means completely new, never used.

The Underwater World.q: Writing a long research paper is a ______ task.
The Underwater World.e: Time-consuming describes a task that takes a lot of time and effort.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: How do some deep-sea animals attract prey in complete darkness?
o: They change their color to white.
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: The text says deep-sea animals use glow-producing organs to attract prey.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: What can sharks detect from miles away?
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: Sharks can detect a single drop of blood from miles away.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: Why are many shark species endangered?
o: because they are dangerous to humans
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: Many species are endangered because of overfishing and pollution.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called ______ .
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: The text says coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps.
They support thousands of species and are often referred to as the rainforests of the sea.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: What problem do baby sea turtles face after hatching?
o: sharks smell them from miles away
they are too big to swim
a hard-to-survive journey to the sea
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: After hatching, baby turtles face a hard-to-survive journey to the sea, and many do not make it.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: "If we turn a blind eye to the damage..." means if we ______ .
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: To turn a blind eye means to ignore something; the text warns against ignoring ocean damage.

Into the Depth of the Ocean.q: Which of these is a compound adjective from the text?
Into the Depth of the Ocean.e: Awe-inspiring is a hyphenated compound adjective used in the text.

Ocean Legends and Storytelling.q: In the beginning of a short story, the writer should ______ .
o: introduce the characters and set the time and place
Ocean Legends and Storytelling.e: The Beginning introduces the main characters, sets the time and place and shows the situation.

Ocean Legends and Storytelling.q: Which tenses are usually used in a short story?
Ocean Legends and Storytelling.e: The Useful Tools say: usually use past simple and past continuous.

Ocean Legends and Storytelling.q: Adding tension or surprise belongs to the ______ of the story.
Ocean Legends and Storytelling.e: The Middle shows the action or conflict and adds tension or surprise.

Ocean Legends and Storytelling.q: Which group contains linking words useful for stories?
